svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4 with 400G ZR/ZR+ support (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G
svg.data-optics-qsfp56: 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: 10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'); the HIG recommends Cat 5e for the RJ45 OOB port and names no SFP+ optic, so no specific module list is published for this pair
svg.data-zr-capacity: up to 4 OpenZR+ transceivers in a front-to-back airflow build and up to 2 in a back-to-front build, and OpenZR+ modules must not sit in adjacent ports (HIG Port Overview, Figures 12 and 13)
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232, 115200 8N1, no flow control (labelled IOIOI)
svg.data-oob: 1x RJ45 100/1000M plus 2x SFP+ 10G, both types reaching the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A

The back-to-front build (FAN-405637-CD with PSU-132-AESR, blue handles, photographed in -3-view) is orderable and not modelled, because the shared PSU and fan components carry only red-latch skins; no chassis SKU appears in any held document (see the chassis-sku gap)","kind":"orderable"},"base":{"airflow":"front-to-back","default":true,"kind":"base","source":"derived - built from the group roles rather than from a vendor bundle: the service bays (six fans, two PSUs) keep their seats and every traffic cage is empty, which is how this switch ships before optics are chosen. UfiSpace publishes no base configuration for this chassis, so the library defines one. The AC supply is the seat because the bay defaults name it; see the ac and dc configurations for the orderable variants."},"dc":{"airflow":"front-to-back","bays":{"psu-0":"ufispace/psu-132-dc@1","psu-1":"ufispace/psu-132-dc@1"},"component-attrs":{"fan-405637":{"model":"FAN-405637-HD"},"psu-132-dc":{"model":"PSU-132-DISB"}},"description":"Dual 1300W DC PSUs (PSU-132-DISB, screw-terminal input, 60A fast-acting internal fuse per the HIG DC procedure) with front-to-back airflow fans (FAN-405637-HD)","kind":"orderable"}},"datasheet":{"title":"UfiSpace S9301-32DB 200/400G Data Center Spine & Leaf Switch Datasheet","url":"https://www.ufispace.com/products/datacenter/200g/s9301-32db-200g-data-center-spine-leaf-switch"},"description":"UfiSpace S9301-32DB 200/400G data center spine and leaf switch - 1RU white box, 24x QSFP56 200G and 8x QSFP-DD 400G in two rows plus a 2x SFP+ 10G out-of-band pair and an RJ45/USB/console management stack, Broadcom Trident4-X9 at 8 Tbps; six hot-swap fans (5+1) and dual 1300W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable in AC or DC and in front-to-back or back-to-front airflow","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"The HIG's section 10 tables the five system lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the RJ45 management jack, and says nothing about the port lamps: not what the four green lamps above each QSFP56 cage mean, not what the four lamps in each QSFP-DD light-pipe strip mean, and not what the single lamp beside each SFP+ cage signals. Four lamps on a four-lane QSFP56 and four on an eight-lane QSFP-DD is suggestive and is not a statement anybody has made. Every port lamp keeps the off/on component default rather than an invented vocabulary.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp56-200g","qsfpdd-400g","sfp-plus-mgmt","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The front render resolves this faceplate's cage column pitch at 19.00 mm with the cages abutting, and the QSFP-DD half of the same row measures the same 19.00 - which is std/qsfp-dd@1's MSA width exactly. std/qsfp56@1 is 20.0 mm wide on provenance that says 'assumed = QSFP28 bezel opening', so two of them cannot sit in one group of this device without colliding. The QSFP56 ports therefore carry std/qsfp-ganged@1 (18.5 mm, the standard per-port opening inside a continuous QSFP block) and the media lives on the group. Either std/qsfp56@1's assumed width is wrong for real hardware or this vendor's QSFP56 cages are narrower than the assumption; nothing held here settles which, and the component was not edited from inside a device task.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["qsfp56-200g"],"wanted":"a QSFP56 panel-cutout dimension from SFF-8661/SFF-8663 or a UfiSpace mechanical drawing","what":"qsfp56-cage-aperture"},{"note":"The HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 43.4 x 100 x 40 mm (W x D x H); the rear render shows six equal fan faces filling 12.5 to 319 mm with no visible chassis web, a measured 51.16 mm pitch, and the shared component measures its face at 50.7 mm. The same table's PSU width, 50.5 mm, matches its drawn face exactly, which makes the fan row the outlier rather than the render. The likely resolution is that 43.4 measures the fan BODY behind the face, but that is an inference; the manifest carries the 50.7 mm face on the measured pitch.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/fan-405637@1","fans"],"wanted":"a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-405637, or a caliper on the FRU","what":"fan-face-width"},{"note":"The HIG's AC Version procedure specifies the cord as IEC60320 C15, 250 VAC 15 A, and a C15 cord mates a C16 appliance inlet - the notched high-temperature variant of the C14 that the shared PSU component composes (std/c14-inlet). The rear render shows the inlet but not at a zoom that resolves the notch.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["ufispace/psu-132-ac@1"],"wanted":"a close-up photograph or drawing of the PSU-132 AC inlet","what":"ac-inlet-standard"},{"note":"No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and HIG name only S9301-32DB, and the ordering lines name only the PSUs and fans. Per the S9510-28DC precedent, whose SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no PDF, orderable SKUs for the AC/DC and airflow variants exist somewhere; the configurations therefore carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["base","ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs","what":"chassis-sku"},{"note":"The five rail attachment pins per side are described in words by the HIG and drawn without dimensions in Figure 18, so they are placed evenly and marked estimated, as are the left-side grounding holes, the compliance label on the underside and the depth extents of the three stadium recesses on the top cover (the footprint drawing they come from is not to scale in its depth axis).","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["left","right","bottom","top"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace mechanical drawing, or square-on photographs of the sides and underside","what":"side-and-underside-detail"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"5+1","redundancy-note":"5+1 - 5+1 hot-swappable (attrs fan-redundancy)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster at the left edge of the face - the RS-232 console RJ45, the USB 3.0 service port, the out-of-band RJ45 and the recessed reset button","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port - the twenty-four green lane quads of the QSFP56 rows, the thirty-two lamps in the four QSFP-DD light-pipe strips and the two SFP+ lamps","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 active-active hot-swappable"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp56-200g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp56","speed":"200g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus-mgmt":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the stacked SFP+ pair the vendor numbers 0 and 1 and marks with the network symbol - the second out-of-band path to the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the chassis indicators - SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and the blue ID beacon","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9301-32DB","name":"s9301-32db","portfolio":{"family":"Data Center Switch","line":"Cloud & Data Centers"},"provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental and Regulatory Compliance sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied.","cage-parts":"registry, with one substitution recorded - the QSFP-DD ports use std/qsfp-dd@1, whose 19.0 mm aperture is exactly the measured 19.00 mm column pitch. The QSFP56 ports use std/qsfp-ganged@1 (18.5 x 9.58, the standard per-port opening inside a continuous QSFP block, which is what abutting cages are) rather than std/qsfp56@1: that part is 20.0 mm wide on its own 'assumed = QSFP28 bezel opening' provenance, 1.0 mm wider than this faceplate's pitch, so two of them in one group would collide. The media and speed are carried by the qsfp56-200g group instead of by the cage part. See the qsfp56-cage-aperture gap.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 1RU, 436 x 645 x 43.8mm', weight 11.2 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple and the same weight. 436 is the body between the ear planes, not a rack face - the HIG Space Clearance section says the S9301-32DB 'width is 17.17 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', so the mounting hardware is additional to 436 and is not drawn. Depth 645 is the chassis without FRUs; the same section adds 25 mm for fan handles and 38 mm for PSU handles beyond it.","front-layout":"measured - front render at 3.789 px/mm. Left to right: the management cluster (reset pinhole over a RESET legend, a white legend block naming five system lamps with the lamp column beside it, a 3x4 vent field below, and a silver bezel carrying console RJ45 / USB 3.0 / OOB RJ45 stacked), then the single stacked SFP+ pair numbered 0 and 1, then the 32 service ports in eight 2x2 groups. Feature positions are good to about 0.3 mm against the render and are carried as measured.","fru-face-vs-table":"sources-disagree, resolved the same way the S9300-32D resolved it and for the same reason - the HIG table gives the fan module 43.4 x 100 x 40 mm and the PSU 50.5 x 321 x 40 mm, but the rear render shows six equal fan faces on a measured 51.16 mm pitch with no chassis web between them. The PSU's tabled 50.5 matches its drawn face exactly, which is what makes the fan row the odd one out: 43.4 is very likely the fan BODY behind a wider face. The manifest carries the shared component's 50.7 mm face on the measured pitch. See the fan-face-width gap.","led-strips":"measured - sixteen vertical light-pipe bezels, one per cage column, bracketing each 2x2 group: twelve magenta (#652849 sampled from the render) over the QSFP56 columns and four blue (#5790bb) over the QSFP-DD columns. Width 2.9 mm magenta / 3.3 mm blue, taken from the centre-to-centre distance of the two strips that abut at each group boundary rather than from a colour threshold on an antialiased edge; each is split into a top and a bottom segment at y 7.7 and 24.7, 13.4 mm tall, with the port numeral printed in white at the outer end of each segment. They carry no lamps on the QSFP56 columns - the lamps there are the green quads - which is why they are decor and not components.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9301-32DB end of life' - no announcement found; the UfiSpace product page, the S9301-32DB FAQ page and several distributor listings are live. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.","mgmt-block":"measured - reset pinhole centred (9.4, 6.1) with the RESET legend below; a white legend block at x 2.8-7.7, y 12.4-25.7 naming SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID (the panel prints PS0 and PS1; the HIG LED table calls the same two rows PSU0 and PSU1, and the table's wording is what the lamp descriptions carry), five lamps beside it on a 2.7 mm pitch, green for the first four and blue for ID; a 3x4 vent field below at x 2.9-12.6, y 26.8-40.2. The silver bezel at x 14.3-31.5, y 5.9-38.6 holds three connectors: console RJ45 at the top (6.5-18.5), USB 3.0 (19.3-25.6), OOB RJ45 at the bottom (26.4-38.4). THE TWO JACKS MIRROR - at 36x zoom the console shows its latch keyway UP with the eight contacts below, and the OOB shows the contacts UP with the keyway below, so the console is rotate: 180 and the OOB is not. The 12.7 x 11.0 mm ganged-RJ45 cells (std/rj45-ganged@2, via common/rj45-ganged-eth@1) are used because the 15.8 x 13.2 mm single-housing jack (std/rj45@2) does not fit: two of those plus the 7.0 mm-tall common/usb-a@2 between them stack to 33.4 mm in a 32.7 mm bezel. common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 draws its two integrated lamps on the keyway side already, matching the photo; the mismatch common/rj45-hd@1 used to force (its lamps drawn on the CONTACT side, against this device's keyway-side photo) is gone, and the jack stays unrotated because the contacts and keyway are geometry, unaffected by the lamp side.","part-numbers":"The FRU part numbers (PSU-132-DESR/DISB/AESR/AISB, FAN-405637-HD/CD) are datasheet ordering lines and live on the configurations. NO ORDERABLE CHASSIS SKU appears in any held document - the datasheet and HIG name the product only as S9301-32DB. The S9510-28DC lesson applies: such SKUs exist at the owner even when no held PDF prints one, so this is recorded as a gap rather than as 'no SKU exists'. The back-to-front airflow build (blue handles and latches: FAN-405637-CD with PSU-132-AESR/DESR) is orderable and photographed in -3-view but is not modelled as a configuration, because the shared PSU and fan components carry only red-latch skins.","port-grid":"measured - the 48 green lane lamps of the top cage row give the column geometry directly: column 0 centre 82.08 mm, column pitch 19.00 mm inside a group, group pitch 45.05 mm, fitted over all twelve QSFP56 columns with a maximum residual of 0.3 mm. The sixteen LED-strip bezels fall at column centre -/+ 11.25 mm (predicted against measured: 70.83/70.60, 112.33/112.56, ... 427.33/427.69), which is the check that the two independent feature families agree. Cage rows: openings measured 11.74-20.27 and 26.00-34.44 mm, so the row centres are 16.00 and 30.22 mm and the parts are centred on them. The BOTTOM row is drawn rotate: 180 - the cage latch notch sits at the top of the top row and the bottom of the bottom row in both the render and the HIG figure, the belly-to-belly pattern. Numbering from HIG Figure 11 and the render's own white numerals: each column carries an even port on top and the odd one below it, left to right, 0..23 on the QSFP56 columns and 24..31 on the four QSFP-DD columns, and the HIG Port Overview table agrees ('Port ID 0~23 QSFP56 200/100G, 24~31 QSFP-DD 400/200/100G'). The HIG Overview prose says '24 x 200GE QSFP56 and 32 x 400GE QSFP-DD ports', which totals 56 on a 32-port faceplate and is a copy-paste error in that sentence; the table, the datasheet and both figures all say 24 + 8.","port-leds":"measured - the two port families carry DIFFERENT indicators, and reading one rule across both would have been wrong. Each QSFP56 port has four round green lamps in a horizontal row, above the cage on the top row and below it on the bottom row (48 lamps counted across the top row, 4.05 mm pitch measured, lamp rows centred at y 8.45 and 38.14) - ufispace/lane-led-quad@1, whose own 3.94 mm pitch is 2.7% tighter and is left alone. Each QSFP-DD port instead has four lamps in a VERTICAL column inside its blue light-pipe strip, at y 12.27/14.56/16.85/19.14 on the top row and 26.76/29.11/31.46/33.81 on the bottom, 1.3 mm across - drawn as four common/led-dot@1 because the library's vertical strip part (ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-2x4@1, 5.6 mm wide, two columns) is wider than the 3.3 mm strip this device gives one column and would land on the neighbouring cage.","power":"datasheet 'Typical power: 291.6 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare; the HIG's Connecting Power section states 'The maximum system power consumption is 892.9 watts' in BOTH the DC and the AC procedure, unqualified as to optics, carried as power-max-w. The two figures are two documents' claims and are not reconciled against each other or against the module set. PSU rating 1300 W per supply (datasheet ordering lines); the HIG asks for 'a reserve of at least 1300 watts on each power circuit' for the active-active feed.","rear-layout":"measured - rear render (-4-view, front-to-back red FRUs) at 1660 px / 436 mm = 3.807 px/mm. Six fan bays and two PSU bays. The fan pitch is 51.16 mm, fitted over the six fan status lamps at 61.59, 112.68, 163.76, 214.98, 266.20 and 317.41 mm (residuals under 0.15 mm) and confirmed independently by the six red release latches at 60.81, 112.02, 163.24, 214.46, 265.54 mm; bays are drawn at the shared component's 50.7 mm face from x 12.5, so fan 5 ends at 319.0 and the PSUs follow. PSU0 at 320.5 and PSU1 at 378.0, each 50.5 mm wide - the HIG's own PSU width - leaving a 7.0 mm chassis strip after PSU0 and 7.5 mm after PSU1, which is where the vertical PSU0 and PSU1 legends are printed (measured at x 374.5 and 431.5). The grounding column at the left edge carries two M4 lug holes at (6.4, 7.6) and (6.4, 22.6) and the earth symbol at (6.4, 35.4); HIG Figure 27 shows the two-hole grounding lug seated exactly there. The FAN and PSU numbers are position facts and are chassis silkscreen, not marks on the interchangeable FRU. THE FAN NUMBERS ARE LIFTED: the render prints 'FAN \u25c4N' at y 3.5-9 on the fan's own tab strip, and HIG Figure 21 shows that strip - screw, latch and lamp with it - coming out with the module, so a legend drawn there would be painted over by the seated fan and would be invisible in every configuration. They are printed instead in the 1.9 mm chassis strip above the bays, where the S9300-32D puts them, and the x centres are the measured ones. The two grounding holes are drawn with the silver ring the render shows around each, because a bare dark hole on a dark rear reads as nothing at all. This rear differs slightly from the library's S9300-32D, which shares the same 436 x 645 x 43.8 body and the same PSU-132 and FAN-405637 FRUs but was modelled at a 51.56 mm fan pitch with PSUs at 321.0/381.4 off a lower-resolution guide figure; the numbers here are measured from THIS device's own render and are not inherited.","sfp-block":"measured - one stacked pair of SFP+ cages, not two columns, centred x 42.95 with the cage rows on the same centrelines as the QSFP rows (16.00 and 30.22). THEY MIRROR: the upper cage carries its two contact blocks at the top and its latch tab at the bottom edge, the lower one the reverse, so the lower is rotate: 180. One green lamp and one white numeral sit outside each cage - lamp at x 40.4 and numeral at x 44.5, on the same two baselines as the QSFP56 lamp rows (8.45 and 38.14). The datasheet calls these '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports' and the HIG's Connecting the OOB Management Cables section calls them the second of two OOB port types that reach the x86, both marked with the network symbol - which the render prints above the pair.","sources":"UfiSpace S9301-32DB datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9301-32db-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, power, environment and compliance; S9301-32DB Hardware Installation Guide (s9301-32db-hig) for the system-overview and port-overview figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables, grounding and rack mounting; four vendor product renders (photos/s9301-32db-1-view isometric, -2-view front, -3-view rear with back-to-front blue FRUs, -4-view rear with front-to-back red FRUs) for colour, counts, orientation and construction. THE FRONT GEOMETRY IN THIS FILE IS MEASURED OFF THE FRONT RENDER, not off the HIG figure: the render draws the chassis face across 1652 px (px 11 to 1662, the side attachment pins protruding beyond it on both sides) for 436 mm = 3.789 px/mm, and 166 px for 43.8 mm = 3.790 px/mm, so it is isotropic to 0.03% and resolves features the HIG figure blurs. The HIG Figure 11 port overview was gated too and passes (1377 x 138 px, aspect 9.978 against the true 9.954, 0.24% out); it agrees with the render on every pitch below and is the source for the port NUMBERING, which the render prints too small to read at some strips.","views":"Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 5, whose footprint drawing prints the fan handles and PSUs at the top; the three shallow stadium recesses are proportioned off that drawing and their y extents are ESTIMATED, because the drawing's depth axis is not to scale - it draws 436 x 645 at aspect 0.977 against a true 0.676 - while their x extents are fractions of a width the same drawing gets right. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG rack-mounting section describes ('The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins'), evenly spaced and ESTIMATED - no held drawing dimensions them; the left side near the rear carries the second designated grounding location, which HIG Figure 26 shows under a yellow REMOVE LABEL FOR SYSTEM GROUNDING tag, hole positions estimated. Apart from that grounding pair the side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature."},"references":[{"title":"UfiSpace S9301-32DB Hardware Installation Guide"}],"version":"2.0.1","views":{"bottom":{"components":{"placements":[{"at":[108,220],"group":"furniture","id":"bottom-label","ref":"common/compliance-sticker@1","rel-pos":1}]},"size":{"h":645,"w":436}},"front":{"components":{"placements":[{"at":[7.4,4.1],"for":"chassis","group":"mgmt","id":"reset","ref":"common/reset-button@1","rel-pos":4},{"at":[7.6,12.35],"description":"HIG Front Panel LED table, SYS row - Off (no power), Solid Green (host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but host CPU/BMC boot failed)","for":"chassis","group":"status-leds","id":"led-sys","ref":"common/led-rect@1","rel-pos":1,"states":["off",{"color":"#22c55e","name":"ok"},{"color":"#f59e0b","name":"boot-failed"}]},{"at":[7.6,15.05],"description":"HIG Front Panel LED table, FAN row - Off (fans are not initialized), Solid Green (all fans are work normal), Blinking Amber (fan fail: one or more fans need service)","for":["rear/fan-0","rear/fan-1","rear/fan-2","rear/fan-3","rear/fan-4","rear/fan-5"],"group":"status-leds","id":"led-fan","ref":"common/led-rect@1","rel-pos":2,"states":["off",{"color":"#22c55e","name":"ok"},{"behavior":"blinking","color":"#f59e0b","name":"fault"}]},{"at":[7.6,17.75],"description":"HIG Front Panel LED table, PSU0 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU0 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 needs service). g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, SYS row - Off (no power), Solid Green (host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but host CPU/BMC boot failed)
g.title: led-sys

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, FAN row - Off (fans are not initialized), Solid Green (all fans are work normal), Blinking Amber (fan fail: one or more fans need service)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, PSU0 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU0 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 needs service). The panel silkscreen abbreviates the row to PS0
g.title: led-ps0

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, PSU1 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU1 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU1 fail, PSU1 needs service). The panel silkscreen abbreviates the row to PS1
g.title: led-ps1

g.data-description: HIG Front Panel LED table, ID row - Off (no power), Blinking Blue (beacon feature is enabled on the switch)
g.title: led-id

g.data-description: HIG Initial System Setup - the console is the RJ45 port labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1, no flow control. Drawn rotate 180 because this jack shows its latch keyway up and its contacts down, the mirror of the OOB jack below it
g.title: console

g.data-description: HIG Management Port LED table - left lamp Off (no power), Solid Green (1G link-up), Blinking Green (1G TX/RX activity); right lamp Off (no power), Solid Amber (10M/100M link-up), Blinking Amber (10M/100M TX/RX activity). The two lamps do not share a vocabulary, so they are declared per element
g.title: oob

g.data-description: the stacked SFP+ pair the vendor numbers 0 and 1 and marks with the network symbol - the second out-of-band path to the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)
g.title: port-sfp-0

g.data-description: the stacked SFP+ pair the vendor numbers 0 and 1 and marks with the network symbol - the second out-of-band path to the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)
g.title: port-sfp-1
